sentences.text: 2 The Chao family are in the Museum They are talking about what they have just seen.
Listen and fill in The missing information in the spaces below.
The first one has been provided as an example.
You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers.
So what did you two see?
We saw an exhibition on teenagers and comics of the world.
Was it interesting?
Oh yeah. It was brilliant!
There are loads of comics just for girls.
Really? I never knew that.
I thought all the comics would be for boys.
That’s what I thought too.
But there are so many for girls particularly Japanese comics.
Oh really? What are they like?
Are they violent?
Violent? Of course not, Mum.
Duh! I said comics for girls, not boys.
So what are they like then?
Well, there are two main kinds of comics for girls.
The first kind’s fantasy.
What kind of fantasy?
Can you give me an example?
OK. I suppose the most popular kind is a superhero comic.
And what about the other kind?
Well, the other main kind’s real life, for example school life.
You seem to know a lot about comic books.
Oh yeah. I read them all the time.
I didn’t know that!
Where do you buy them?
There’s a shop I go to in Electric Road.
Electric Road? Why do you go there?
Why not a place near our home?
There’s a much better choice there.
I’m not sure I like the idea of you buying comics.
Oh, it’s not what you think.
These are comic books for teenagers.
They’re not violent at all.
They’re about problems teenagers have.
Problems teenagers have?
Like what? Arguing with parents.
I mean, we’re arguing now.
That’s a problem for me.
Ha ha. Very funny.
Look you too.
Let’s stop this.
What did you see, Linda?
I saw an exhibition on best -selling toys from the past.
Oh, That sounds interesting.
What did they have?
Well, one of the things they had was a Cabbage -patched Doll.
It was really popular in the 1980s.
That doesn’t sound very exciting.
Ah, but this doll is actually really ugly.
Really? Why would anyone want a doll like that?
But that’s the whole point.
People bought the doll because it was ugly.
I really can’t believe that.
How many little girls would want one?
Well actually, millions of little girls.
Why were they so popular?
Well, I think it’s because there were many different designs.
Many different designs?
Yes, and this made them very collectible.
So ugly but collectible dolls.
Do you want one for your birthday, Angela?
Actually, I’d quite like one.
I can look after it for a few years so it increases in price.
That’s my girl!
Always thinking ahead.
What else did you see, Linda?
Um, I saw one other thing that I think you would really like.
Which is? A space hopper.
A what? A space hopper.
is like a big rubber ball.
A big rubber ball?
Yes, and you sit on it and jump around.
Wow, jumping around.
That sounds kind of fun.
But the best part was the extra things you know, the other things that kids used to do with space hoppers.
Like what? Well, you can have a race.
Actually, me and my brother both had one and as well as having races it was really good fun having a fight.
late. You and your brother fighting.
That doesn’t surprise me.
Actually, this toy is beginning to sound awesome.
Can we go back and see it, Mum?
Sure, let’s go.
